notes: Prose revision against the house standards for plain, declarative scientific writing, together with the correction of two numerical errors. The manuscript was reread in full and rewritten paragraph by paragraph. Aphoristic section titles were replaced ('The planner who was right' became 'Introduction'; 'Identical intelligence, eighty-one to one' became 'Distribution under identical intelligence'; 'Where the fallback argument is right, and where it stops' became 'Human fallback after automated incident response'). First-person singular under the institutional byline was removed ('and, I think, worth hitting', 'The last point is the one I would keep'), as were self-reference ('This paper calls', 'the sharpest thing in the paper'), meta-commentary ('It also has to be said plainly', 'three things about this limit are worth separating', 'that should be said first'), epigrams ('The best forecast is not the legitimate constitution', 'is a claim about failure independence dressed as a claim about biology', 'What they are owed was never going to be settled by finding them a residual job description'), and 'rather than' (seven to none). The closing argument about the allocation result was kept and restated plainly. The Endsley and Kiris sentence remains limited to what the title establishes, since the full text was never retrieved. Two published numbers were wrong and are corrected. The containment crossing was reported as 50 percent automation, which was the first grid point evaluated past the crossing; the responder's success is linear in the automated share and the exact crossing is 43.2 percent. The independence requirement was reported as 0.341, the largest grid value below the bound; the exact bound is 0.352. Both are now computed in closed form, bound in the claim ledger to the new fields, and protected by invariants that check the exact values against the grid. The claim ledger was re-bound and all 23 claims pass.
